# Budget for Japan, limit $3000

## FX
1 USD = 157.89 JPY on 2026-09-18 (Frankfurter)

## Category split (target)
| Category | Share | USD | JPY |
| stay | 35% | 1050 | 165,800 |
| transport | 15% | 450 | 71,050 |
| food | 25% | 750 | 118,400 |
| activities | 15% | 450 | 71,050 |
| buffer | 10% | 300 | 47,400 |

## Price bands (estimates unless marked tool)
| Item | Low USD | High USD | Basis | Source |
| Hotel night, quiet area, 3-star | 80 | 150 | 1 traveller, Tokyo/Kyoto mid-range | estimate |
| Shinkansen Tokyo-Kyoto one way | 100 | 140 | reserved seat, per person | estimate |
| Meals per day (street + one sit-down) | 30 | 55 | 1 traveller, food-focused trip | estimate |
| Temple entry each | 3 | 10 | most major temples charge in this range | estimate |
| Local transit per day | 8 | 15 | subway/bus day pass, Tokyo and Kyoto | estimate |

## If over budget, cut here (in order)
1. Move Tokyo stay from a central ward like Shibuya or Ginza to a quieter area like Asakusa or Nippori, saves about $30 to $50 per night.
2. Swap one Shinkansen reserved seat for a non-reserved (jiyuseki) car on off-peak trains, saves about $10 to $20 per trip.
3. Cut one sit-down dinner per two days in favour of a second street-food or convenience-store meal, saves about $15 to $20 per day.
4. Skip paid temple grounds beyond the main hall (many temples charge extra for inner gardens), saves about $3 to $8 per site.
5. Use a multi-day subway pass instead of single tickets in Kyoto, saves about $2 to $4 per day.
